settings.title: Audio Quick Editor Settings
settings.summary: Tune quick inline audio edits while keeping original Anki media untouched.
settings.tabs.label: Settings sections
settings.presets.title: Processing presets
settings.presets.summary: Here you can create a sequence of audio operations and save it as a preset. For example, you can denoise the audio, shorten pauses, and then make it louder.
settings.presets.name: Name
settings.presets.name.tooltip: Name this preset so it is easy to find in the editor and Browser batch tools.
settings.presets.duplicate.tooltip: Copy this preset before experimenting with changes.
settings.presets.delete.tooltip: Delete this preset from Settings, editor quick actions, Browser batch, and trigger choices.
settings.presets.steps_summary: Run transform steps in order, then optionally draw a graph from the result.
settings.presets.add_step.tooltip: Add the selected operation to the end of this preset.
settings.presets.add_step_operation.tool: Choose the operation you want to add next.
settings.presets.list_item.tooltip: Click a preset here to edit its name, steps, and graph output.
settings.presets.move_up.tooltip: Run this step earlier in the preset.
settings.presets.move_down.tooltip: Run this step later in the preset.
settings.presets.remove_step.tooltip: Remove this step from the preset.
settings.presets.operation.tooltip: Choose what this step does to the audio.
settings.presets.graph_enabled.tooltip: Create a pitch and intensity graph after the audio edits finish.
settings.presets.validation.empty_preset: {name} needs at least one step or graph output.
settings.triggers.title: Trigger rules
settings.triggers.summary: Create rules that run audio operations automatically when you add or edit notes.
settings.triggers.name: Name
settings.triggers.name.tooltip: Name this rule so you can recognize it later.
settings.triggers.enabled.tooltip: Turn this rule on or off without deleting it.
settings.triggers.event.tooltip: Choose when this rule should run: when you add a note or when you edit one.
settings.triggers.note_type.tooltip: Choose the note type this rule applies to.
settings.triggers.source_field.tooltip: Choose the field that contains the audio you want to process.
settings.triggers.action.tooltip: Choose what should happen automatically: one quick operation or a saved preset.
settings.triggers.preset.tooltip: Choose the saved preset this trigger should run.
settings.triggers.target_field.tooltip: Choose where to put the graph if this action creates one.
settings.triggers.list_item.tooltip: Click a rule here to edit when it runs and what it does.
settings.triggers.duplicate.tooltip: Make a copy of this rule so you can change it safely.
settings.triggers.operation.tooltip: Choose the one audio operation this rule should run.
settings.voice_recording_countdown_secon: Shows a countdown after you click the Record button.
settings.share_target.catbox.tooltip:
Permanent public upload while the Catbox service keeps it available.
Use this when you want a link that should last.
settings.share_target.litterbox.tooltip:
Temporary public upload that expires after about 3 days.
Use this for quick sharing when the link does not need to last.
settings.selection_marker_shift_buttons_: Two small buttons allow you to jump from marker to marker, so that you can repeat words more easily.
settings.toolbar_visibility.title: Editor toolbar buttons
settings.toolbar_visibility.summary: Choose which quick editor buttons are shown beside audio fields.
Removes noise and sometimes background music.
settings.toolbar_visibility.icon_tooltip: Show this toolbar item as an icon instead of text.
settings.toolbar_visibility.show_panel_t: Show this toolbar panel in the editor.
settings.toolbar_visibility.show_tooltip: Show this toolbar item in the editor.
settings.toolbar_visibility.hidden_setti: Settings remain available from Tools -> Anki Audio Quick Editor -> Settings.
Illustration showing the hidden Settings button
settings.toolbar_visibility.mode_locked_: This display setting is locked because the button belongs to a grouped toolbar panel.
settings.graph_smoothness.tooltip: Choose how smooth the graph should look. Smoother graphs are easier to read, while raw graphs show more detail.
graph.smoothness.raw.tooltip:
Least smoothed graph.
Shows the most detail, but the pitch line can have many sharp angles.
graph.smoothness.balanced.tooltip:
Good default for most speech.
Keeps visible detail while reducing small jagged changes.
graph.smoothness.smooth.tooltip:
Cleaner graph for reading overall intonation.
Hides more tiny bends and angles.
graph.smoothness.very_smooth.tooltip:
Smoothest graph.
Best when you only need the broad pitch movement, not every small corner.
settings.graph_connect_short_dropouts_ms: Connect holes in graph shorter than (ms)
graph.voice_range.note: Who is speaking on the recording? How low or high is the voice you hear?
graph.voice_range.bass.tooltip:
Lowest adult voices.
Example: deep male narration or a bass singer.
graph.voice_range.low.tooltip:
Lower voices.
Example: most adult male speech.
graph.voice_range.general.tooltip:
Middle-range voices.
Example: mixed speakers or any clip where you are not sure yet.
graph.voice_range.high.tooltip:
Higher voices.
Example: many adult female voices.
graph.voice_range.child.tooltip:
Highest voices.
Example: children, teens, or strong falsetto.
graph.recording_condition.note: How noisy or echoey is the recording around the speaker?
graph.recording_condition.auto.tooltip: Lets the analyzer guess the best setting for this clip.
graph.recording_condition.very_noisy.too:
For heavy background noise.
Example: street traffic, train noise, cafe chatter, or strong fan hiss.
graph.recording_condition.noisy.tooltip:
For noticeable noise.
Example: classroom recordings, office hum, or distant chatter.
graph.recording_condition.normal.tooltip:
For everyday recordings.
Example: phone speech in a mostly quiet room.
graph.recording_condition.clean.tooltip:
For clean close-mic audio.
Example: headset speech or a quiet study room.
graph.recording_condition.studio.tooltip:
For very clean recordings.
Example: treated room audio or a studio microphone.
graph.connect_dropouts.note: Bridges tiny missing gaps when the pitch line disappears for a moment.
graph.voice_lock.note: How much should the pitch line ignore quick jumps and stay on the same voice?
graph.voice_lock.loose.tooltip:
Follows quick jumps more easily.
Use this when you want more detail, even if the line looks jumpy.
graph.voice_lock.balanced.tooltip:
Keeps natural changes but filters some sudden jumps.
Good default for most speech.
graph.voice_lock.stable.tooltip:
Ignores more sudden jumps and keeps the line steadier.
Use this when the graph keeps hopping between harmonics.
settings.ffmpeg_path.help: Prefilled with a platform default. Change it if your ffmpeg binary lives elsewhere.
settings.dpdfnet_attn_limit_db.tooltip: Choose how strongly DPDFNet reduces noise. Stronger settings remove more noise but can change the voice more.
settings.dpdfnet_attn_limit_db.gentle.to:
Light cleanup.
Use when the recording is already clear and you want fewer artifacts.
settings.dpdfnet_attn_limit_db.normal.to:
Balanced cleanup.
Good default when noise is present but the voice is still clear.
settings.dpdfnet_attn_limit_db.aggressiv:
Strong cleanup.
Use when noise is distracting, but expect a higher chance of metallic artifacts.
settings.speed_step.tooltip: Choose the speed factor for this operation.
settings.speed_step.slower.tooltip: How many times slower should the audio become?
settings.speed_step.faster.tooltip: How many times faster should the audio become?
settings.volume_step_db.tooltip: Choose how many decibels each volume step should add or remove.
settings.pause_aggressiveness.tooltip: Choose how boldly the pause remover cuts silence.
settings.pause_detection_algorithm.toolt: Choose how pauses are detected before they are shortened.
settings.pause_detection_algorithm.silen:
Uses ffmpeg silence detection with optional denoise preprocessing.
Good default for noisy cards.
settings.pause_detection_algorithm.siler:
Uses a speech detector trained to separate voice from silence.
Often faster and better for normal speech clips.
settings.pause_threshold_db.help: How quiet audio must be before ffmpeg treats it as silence. Use a less negative value, for example -35 dB, when background music or room noise should not be cut as a pause.
settings.pause_threshold_probability.hel: How confident Silero must be that a frame is speech. Raise it, for example from 0.50 to 0.80, when background music or noise is being mistaken for speech.
settings.pause_min_silence_seconds.help: The shortest detected pause that can be removed. Increase it to keep small natural gaps; decrease it to cut quick hesitations.
settings.pause_min_speech_seconds.help: The shortest speech or sound island that protects a gap from being merged into one pause. Increase it to preserve short words or breaths between pauses.
settings.pause_preprocess_denoise.help: Runs denoise before detection only. Pause cuts are still rendered from the original audio, so this helps analysis without changing the kept sound.
settings.output_format.tooltip: Choose the audio format this step should write.
settings.size_reduction_mode.gentle.tool:
Keeps stereo and normal sample rates when possible.
Best when you only need modest savings.
settings.size_reduction_mode.normal.tool:
Good default for phone review clips.
Uses lower bitrate and mono when safe.
Smallest files with more audible quality loss.
Useful for throwaway or very space-constrained decks.
settings.size_reduction_bitrate_kbps.hel: Sets the MP3 bitrate cap passed as -b:a. The renderer still avoids increasing known source bitrate.
settings.size_reduction_sample_rate_hz.h: Sets the sample-rate cap passed as -ar. The renderer omits upsampling when the source is already lower.
settings.size_reduction_channels.help: Sets the channel cap passed as -ac. Mono saves the most space; stereo preserves left/right separation.
settings.denoise_algorithm.tooltip: Choose the noise reduction engine for this step.
settings.denoise_algorithm.standard.tool:
General cleanup for everyday background noise.
Start here for most recordings.
settings.denoise_algorithm.rnnoise.toolt:
Light, fast speech denoise.
Use it for hiss, fan noise, or low-power machines.
settings.denoise_algorithm.voice_only.to:
Separates the vocals stem from accompaniment with Sherpa Spleeter.
Best for mixed music or backing tracks, and less reliable for spoken-word isolation.

editor.split.description_speed: How much faster or slower to make the audio.
editor.split.description_volume: How much louder or quieter to make the audio.
editor.split.description_denoise: Removes noise and sometimes music from the audio. Different algorithms work better for different kinds of noise.
editor.split.description_share: Share this file online. The link will be copied to the clipboard.
editor.split.description_reduce_size: Compresses to MP3 by reducing bitrate, sample rate, or channels when that is safe.
editor.split.description_graph: To draw an accurate graph, we need to know some details about the speaker and surroundings.
editor.split.description_record_voice: Choose how many seconds to count down before recording starts.
editor.split.description_shorten_pauses: Attempts to remove pauses between sentences.
editor.split.description_pitch_hum: Turns speech into a pitch-preserving hum by removing consonants and vowel differences. Useful for practicing intonation.
editor.split.option.output_format.source: Keep the original file extension when this add-on can safely re-encode to it; otherwise use a compatible fallback.
editor.split.option.output_format.mp3.de: Most portable. Guaranteed to work in AnkiMobile and broadly supported everywhere.
editor.split.option.output_format.m4a.de: Small modern file with good quality, especially on Apple devices.
editor.split.option.output_format.wav.de: Uncompressed and large. Best for temporary editing, not daily review media.
editor.split.option.output_format.flac.d: Lossless and smaller than WAV. Good for archiving, but less portable than MP3.
editor.split.option.pause.gentle.descrip: Removes only longer silences, usually above about 700 ms. Lowest risk of clipping natural rhythm.
editor.split.option.pause.normal.descrip: Shortens common sentence gaps, usually above about 450 ms. Good default for review clips.
editor.split.option.pause.aggressive.des: Cuts shorter pauses too, often above about 150 ms. Can make speech feel rushed.
editor.split.option.pitch_hum.direct.des: Fast mode that follows detected pitch directly.
editor.split.option.pitch_hum.pitch_tier: Uses Praat PitchTier resynthesis when available. More controlled, but slower.
